sources.title: Nitin Nitsure, Construction of Hilbert and Quot Schemes (arXiv:math/0504590)
sources.locator: Sections 1-5, printed pp. 1-30 of the arXiv full text, read in full; Section 6 (variants and applications) not claimed

contents.name: Sec. 1: the functor Hilb_{P^n} of flat closed subschemes over a locally Noetherian base
contents.locator: Sec. 1, definition of Hilb_{P^n} and its functor of points; printed pp. 2-3
contents.support: Embedded closed finite-presentation flat families with scheme-theoretic pullback; the packet's definition keeps this contract and adds the fixed-polynomial subfunctor.

contents.name: Sec. 1: the Quot functor for coherent quotients of a finite sum of twists
contents.reason: The commissioned AG-MOD-1 contract is the Hilbert functor of embedded closed subschemes; general coherent quotients of a finite sum are not promised on this page and the packet deliberately fixes E = O_X.

contents.name: Sec. 1: fpqc descent for the Hilbert and Quot functors
contents.support: The packet proves module and closed-subscheme descent along faithfully flat covers and the open and closed polynomial loci.

contents.name: Sec. 1: explicit Grassmannian construction by affine matrix charts, universal quotient and Plucker determinant embedding
contents.locator: Sec. 1, 'Construction of Grassmannian' through 'Projective embedding'; printed pp. 7-9
contents.support: The matrix-chart gluing, universal quotient and det(U) very ample line are reproduced for coherent sources over a locally Noetherian base.

contents.name: Sec. 1: stratification by Hilbert polynomials, coproduct over polynomials
contents.locator: Sec. 1, 'Stratification by Hilbert Polynomials'; printed pp. 4-5
contents.support: Fixes the Euler-characteristic definition of the fibre polynomial; the local item proves polynomiality for an arbitrary ample polarization and both equivalences.

contents.name: Sec. 1: Snapper's Lemma (polynomiality of the Euler characteristic) cited to Kleiman
contents.locator: Sec. 1, sentence after the Hilbert-polynomial definition; printed p. 4
contents.support: The local item replaces the citation with a complete hyperplane-difference proof, so no external Snapper citation is load-bearing.

contents.name: Sec. 2: definition of m-regularity and the associated hyperplane restriction sequence
contents.locator: Sec. 2, opening definition and exact sequence; printed p. 9
contents.support: The twist convention and zero-sheaf case are recorded; the restriction sequence is proved in the propagation item.

contents.name: Sec. 2 Lemma 2.1 (Castelnuovo): multiplication surjectivity, the vanishing range, and generation
contents.locator: Lemma 2.1 (a)(b)(c) and its proof; printed pp. 9-11
contents.support: Proved with the infinite-field reduction, associated-point hyperplane and simultaneous induction recorded locally.

contents.name: Sec. 2 Remark 2.2: propagation of restriction surjectivity to all larger twists
contents.support: Absorbed into step 2.1 of the uniform-bound item, where equality of two consecutive h^1 values propagates to a contradiction.

contents.name: Sec. 2 Theorem 2.3 (Mumford): uniform regularity bound F_{p,n} for subsheaves of a finite sum of twists
contents.support: Reproduced with an explicit recursive integer R; the printed bound depends on p and n, so the packet adds the ambient-dimension-independent strengthening.

contents.name: Sec. 2 exercises: regularity of O(r) and regularity in short exact sequences
contents.locator: Exercises after Lemma 2.1 and after Theorem 2.3; printed pp. 10-11
contents.reason: These are consistency exercises stating no result the packet promises; the exact-sequence direction is absorbed into the long-exact-sequence steps of the two regularity items.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Lemma 3.1: base change without flatness, with a bound depending on the morphism
contents.reason: The fixed-map Noetherian section-comparison argument is proved inline in universal-flattening steps 1.1 and 3.1 from a two-term twist presentation and Serre vanishing. For its universal arbitrary-test direction, step 4.1 uses the complete uniform-sections-after-flat-pullback theorem, whose cutoff depends only on the presentation and fibre polynomial, not on the test morphism. No additional general map-dependent base-change lemma is needed; the actual fixed-map specialization is retained and proved.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Theorem 3.3 (Grothendieck complex): finite projective complex computing cohomology after every base change
contents.support: The published arbitrary-base version is the packet's supplier; no second local item duplicates it.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Theorem 3.4: representing pi_*(F tensor pi^*G) by Hom(Q,G)
contents.support: Absorbed into steps 1.1-2.1 of the vanishing-locus item, which constructs Q by dualizing the cohomology complex.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Theorem 3.5: representability of the functor Hom(E,F) by a linear scheme
contents.support: The presentation E_1 -> E_0 -> E and the left-exactness argument are reproduced for the universal vanishing locus.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Remark 3.6: the universal vanishing locus as the inverse image of the zero section
contents.support: The closed-subscheme universal property is exactly the vanishing-locus item's statement.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Theorem 3.7: base change for flat sheaves; semicontinuity, locally constant Euler characteristic, constancy implies local freeness
contents.support: The direct-image vanishing, finite local freeness and arbitrary base-change parts are proved across all test schemes; the Euler part is the published locally constant supplier.

contents.name: Sec. 4 Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2: generic flatness
contents.support: The published Noetherian generic-flatness items supply the finite reduced partition used by the universal flattening item.

contents.name: Sec. 4 Theorem 4.3: flattening stratification by Hilbert polynomial (points, universal property, closure order)
contents.support: The scheme-theoretic universal property on arbitrary test schemes and the incoherent-rank-locus gluing are proved locally.

contents.name: Sec. 5: the three projectivity conventions (coherent bundle, vector bundle, projective space)
contents.support: The packet adopts the coherent-projective-bundle convention and separates it from H-projectivity, with no converse asserted.

contents.name: Sec. 5 Theorem 5.1 (Grothendieck): representability of Quot over a Noetherian base for a relatively very ample polarization
contents.support: Proved for an arbitrary chosen relatively ample bundle on each Noetherian affine base, with the substituted-polynomial reduction.

contents.name: Sec. 5 Theorems 5.2-5.3 (Altman-Kleiman): P(V), a coherent quotient of pi^*W(nu), and the closed embedding into P(F)
contents.support: The ambient projective-space construction with one uniformly fixed degree is proved for Noetherian bases.

contents.name: Sec. 5 Lemma 5.4: twist reindexing and the closed embedding cut out by a surjection E -> G
contents.support: The vanishing-subscheme step is absorbed into the construction where the universal kernel is evaluated back to the ideal.

contents.name: Sec. 5 'Use of m-Regularity': uniform bound, generation, locally free direct images, Grassmannian quotient
contents.support: Strengthened to a bound independent of the test algebra, including non-Noetherian targets, via filtered-colimit flatness descent.

contents.name: Sec. 5: construction of the universal family and valuative properness of the Quot scheme
contents.locator: Sec. 5, remainder of the construction; printed pp. 26-30
contents.support: The Grassmannian quotient, flattening stratum, arbitrary-valuation flat closure and coproduct over polynomials assemble the global representation.

contents.name: Sec. 6: some variants and applications (Picard schemes and related constructions)
contents.reason: The binding AG-MOD-1 inventory commissions the Hilbert functor of embedded flat finitely presented subschemes, its representability, universal family, polynomial strata and arbitrary base change. It does not commission general coherent-sheaf Quot representability or the Section 6 quasi-projective Quot, morphism-scheme and equivalence-relation/Picard applications. The local Hilbert construction uses none of those applications.

sources.title: Alexander Grothendieck, Techniques de construction et theoremes d'existence en geometrie algebrique IV: les schemas de Hilbert, Seminaire Bourbaki 221 (1961)
sources.locator: Sections 2 and 3, printed pp. 253-270 of the expose; Section 1 and the introduction are not claimed as read

contents.name: Sec. 2 Theoreme 2.1/2.2: the boundedness criterion, with the printed proof expressly an esquisse
contents.locator: Theoremes 2.1 and 2.2 and the sketch of 2.2 beginning after Corollaire 2.3; printed pp. 255-259
contents.support: Independent original statement of the boundedness criterion; because the printed argument is an esquisse, the packet closes every degree bound with its own recursive b(P) induction and rests nothing on the sketch.

contents.name: Sec. 2 Corollaire 2.3: restriction of the coefficient range to associated-component dimensions
contents.support: The associated-dimension bookkeeping is absorbed into the hyperplane induction on the support dimension.

contents.name: Sec. 2 Lemme 2.4: Chow-coordinate boundedness of reduced subschemes of bounded degree
contents.reason: The Chow-coordinate route to boundedness is not used: the packet proves the uniform regularity bound directly by hyperplane induction, so this key lemma is recorded as the historical alternative.

contents.name: Sec. 2 Lemmes 2.5 and 2.6: bounded quotient modules and coefficient minorations
contents.reason: These lemmas serve only the printed esquisse of the boundedness theorem; the packet's direct regularity induction replaces that route, so they are recorded as history rather than built.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Lemme 3.3: representability of the bounded functors A_nu and the immersion into a Grassmannian
contents.support: Independent confirmation that the representing quotient maps into one Grassmannian by a locally closed immersion.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Lemme 3.4: existence and uniqueness of the subscheme with the local-freeness universal property
contents.support: The universal property for all test schemes is exactly the flattening item's contract.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Lemme 3.5: stabilization of the open rank loci in finite degree ranges
contents.support: Noetherian stabilization is absorbed into intersecting the finitely many rank loci and taking the finite coherent sum of their ideals.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Lemme 3.6: the rank-r locally free locus is a closed subscheme when the rank is constant
contents.support: The full possibly nonreduced closed-subscheme structure is proved locally with Nakayama and a presentation matrix.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Lemme 3.7: unique flat quotient extension over a discrete valuation ring
contents.support: The packet proves the stronger arbitrary-valuation-ring statement required by the published valuative criterion, with the saturated-ideal construction.

contents.name: Sec. 3 Proposition 3.8: relative local freeness and a very ample Grassmannian immersion for the representing quotient
contents.support: The relative very ampleness used for the representative's embedding is proved with the section determinant on each affine base.

sources.title: Alexander Grothendieck, EGA III, Seconde partie (Pub. Math. IHES 17), Chapitre III Section 7.7
sources.locator: Chapitre III, Section 7.7 (7.7.1)-(7.7.9), printed pp. 66-70; exchange setup and theorem statements read in the retrieved scan

contents.name: (7.7.1)-(7.7.3): the exchange functor for a bounded below complex of flat coherent modules and its canonical base-change homomorphism
contents.support: Absorbed into the relative regularity item, which realizes the exchange homomorphism through the finite projective cohomology complex.

contents.name: Theoreme (7.7.5): semicontinuity and the exchange property
contents.support: Independent verification of the vanishing and base-change conclusions proved locally.

contents.name: Theoreme (7.7.6): existence and uniqueness of the coherent module representing pi_*(F tensor pi^*G)
contents.support: Independent verification of the representing module Q built by dualizing the cohomology complex.

contents.name: Corollaires (7.7.7) and (7.7.8): functorial compatibilities and representability for bounded complexes of locally free modules
contents.support: Independent verification that the Hom functor is representable by a linear scheme, yielding the universal vanishing locus.

contents.name: Remarques (7.7.9): base-change formation of the representing module
contents.support: Recorded as the classical base-change statement matching the packet's arbitrary base-change clause.
